changes_made.explanation: Removed redundant dataset entries and normalized model names to consistent format. Kept only instruction-tuned models as they were the main focus of evaluation. Base models were mentioned but not extensively evaluated for NLG tasks.

Consolidated redundant metric names and normalized to standard capitalization. Kept the core evaluation metrics used in the paper: accuracy for correctness, conformity/resistance levels for bias measurement, and confidence/uncertainty metrics for analysis.
No LLMs were used as judges/evaluators in this paper. The LLMs were the subjects being evaluated for conformity behavior, not used to evaluate generated outputs.
No human evaluations were conducted in this study. All evaluations were automated using the metrics described in answer_2.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on evaluating conformity bias in LLMs through automated question-answering experiments. The extraction was generally accurate but contained some redundancy and inconsistent naming. The paper does not use LLMs as judges or conduct human evaluations - all assessments are automated. The core contribution is studying conformity effects in dialogue generation and QA tasks.
